findings.name: Market Value Exclusion for Veterans with a Disability
findings.description: Minnesota does not use a traditional property tax exemption for disabled veterans; instead it excludes a portion of a homesteaded property's market value before tax is calculated. Veterans with a service-connected disability rating of 70% or more (as certified by the VA) qualify for a $150,000 market value exclusion; veterans with a total (100%) and permanent disability qualify for a $300,000 market value exclusion. Property must carry homestead classification and be honorably discharged (DD-214 or other discharge papers required). Applicants in the 70-99% tier must reapply annually; veterans rated 100% permanent and total do not need to reapply after initial approval. Surviving spouses of a 100% permanently and totally disabled veteran may continue to receive the $300,000 exclusion while they receive Dependency and Indemnity Compensation, until they remarry or dispose of the property (a one-time sale still retains the exclusion).
findings.value: $150,000 market value exclusion (70-99% disability); $300,000 market value exclusion (100% permanent and total disability)
otherReqs: Honorably discharged from U.S. armed forces
Property must have homestead classification and be owned/occupied by the veteran (or their primary family caregiver, or qualifying surviving spouse)
Apply to county assessor's office by December 31 of the first assessment year for which the exclusion is sought
70-99% disability tier must reapply annually; 100% permanent and total tier does not reapply after initial approval
findings.agency: Minnesota Department of Revenue / County Assessors
documentation: DD-214 or other official discharge papers
VA certification of service-connected disability rating
findings.sourceExcerpt: for a disability rating of 70 percent or more, $150,000 of market value is excluded... and for a total (100 percent) and permanent disability, $300,000 of market value is excluded... a property owner must apply to the assessor by December 31 of the first assessment year for which the exclusion is sought.

findings.name: Minnesota Veterans Homes
findings.description: Minnesota operates a network of state veterans homes providing 24/7 skilled nursing, domiciliary, and rehabilitative care. An official Minnesota Attorney General veterans-benefits handbook chapter, fetched and read directly this session, confirms at least five homes with listed addresses: Minneapolis, Hastings, Silver Bay, Luverne, and Fergus Falls. Secondary (non-.gov, not independently verified this session) reporting indicates the network expanded to eight homes with new facilities added in Bemidji, Preston, and Montevideo around 2024; that expansion could not be confirmed against a directly-read official mn.gov page in this session because mn.gov/mdva/homes/ and related MDVA CMS pages consistently returned an automated bot-detection challenge page (Radware/ShieldSquare) rather than content on every fetch attempt. The eight-home figure is therefore noted for awareness, not treated as confirmed.
findings.value: Skilled nursing, domiciliary, and rehabilitative care at state veterans homes
otherReqs: Honorable discharge
Minnesota residency
Meets medical/admission criteria set by the individual home (exact admission criteria not printed in the directly-read source; contact facility or County Veteran Service Officer)
findings.agency: Minnesota Department of Veterans Affairs / Minnesota Veterans Homes
documentation: DD-214 or other proof of honorable discharge
findings.sourceExcerpt: Minnesota Veterans Homes Central Office, 5101 Minnehaha Avenue South, Minneapolis... [homes listed with addresses at] Minneapolis, Hastings, Silver Bay, Luverne, Fergus Falls

findings.name: Minnesota GI Bill
findings.description: The Minnesota GI Bill, established in 2007, provides postsecondary financial assistance of up to $15,000 total to eligible veterans, service members with at least five credible years of Minnesota National Guard service since September 11, 2001, and eligible surviving spouses/children of a deceased service member or a veteran with a 100% VA permanent disability who qualify for federal Chapter 33 (Fry Scholarship) or Chapter 35 benefits. Funds can go toward higher education (up to $5,000/academic year), on-the-job training/apprenticeship (up to $2,000/fiscal year, $5,000 aggregate annually), or licenses/certifications (up to $3,000/state fiscal year), as well as admission-test and test-prep costs. Applicants must be Minnesota residents and must reapply annually online at gibill.mn.gov.
findings.value: Up to $15,000 total in postsecondary financial assistance
otherReqs: Minnesota residency
Honorable service in any branch of the U.S. armed forces, OR five credible years cumulative in the Minnesota National Guard since 9/11/2001, OR qualifying surviving spouse/child
Must reapply annually
findings.sourceExcerpt: served honorably in any branch of the United States armed forces at any time... five credible years or more cumulatively as a member of the Minnesota National Guard [since September 11, 2001]... Maximum total benefit: $15,000

findings.name: Minnesota Veterans Preference Act
findings.description: Veterans applying for Minnesota public employment (state, county, city, school district, and other political subdivisions) receive a credit of 10 points added to a passing competitive open-examination score; veterans with a compensable service-connected disability receive a credit of 15 points on open examinations and 5 points on the first promotional examination after initial public employment (disability must be rated 50% or higher for the promotional credit). For Minnesota state agency positions, once minimum qualifications are met, disabled veterans are ranked ahead of non-disabled veterans, who are ranked ahead of non-veterans. Veterans who complete an initial probationary period also receive removal protections (may only be removed for incompetency or misconduct after a hearing). Surviving spouses of deceased veterans, and spouses of disabled veterans unable to qualify, may also claim preference. A veteran denied preference rights may petition the MDVA Commissioner for a hearing before an Administrative Law Judge.
findings.value: 10-point credit for veterans; 15-point credit for disabled veterans (open exams); 5-point credit on first promotional exam
otherReqs: Must achieve a passing score on the examination independent of the preference credit
Compensable service-connected disability (VA or service-branch rating) required for the higher disabled-veteran credit
50%+ disability rating required for the promotional-exam credit
findings.agency: Minnesota Management and Budget / Minnesota Department of Veterans Affairs
documentation: VA or service-branch disability rating letter (for disabled-veteran preference)
findings.sourceExcerpt: a credit of ten points shall be added to the competitive open examination rating... a veteran who has a compensable service-connected disability... shall be given a credit of 15 points... five points... first examination taken for a promotion

findings.name: Military and Veteran Specialty License Plates
findings.description: Minnesota Driver and Vehicle Services offers 22 specialized military/veteran license plate designs (including Disabled American Veterans, Combat Wounded - Purple Heart, Ex-Prisoner of War, Medal of Honor, Gold Star, and multiple campaign/service plates) displayable on passenger vehicles, one-ton pickups, recreational vehicles, and some motorcycles owned or jointly owned by a qualifying veteran. All designs can include the disability parking symbol for qualified applicants and can be personalized. Most plates carry the standard specialty-plate fee ($15.50 for standard plates; $13.50 for motorcycle/recreational-trailer plates), with a $5 transfer fee between vehicles; only Ex-POW, Congressional Medal of Honor, and Gold Star plates are issued with no fee. Applicants must present an original or certified copy of DD-214 discharge papers.
findings.value: 22 specialty plate designs; standard fee $15.50 (auto) / $13.50 (motorcycle/trailer); no fee for Ex-POW, Medal of Honor, and Gold Star plates
otherReqs: Vehicle registration in Minnesota
Documentation of qualifying military/veteran status (DD-214)
findings.agency: Minnesota Department of Public Safety, Driver and Vehicle Services (DVS)
documentation: Original or certified copy of DD-214 or other discharge papers
findings.sourceExcerpt: Military and veteran plates may be displayed on any passenger-class vehicle, one-ton pickup, recreational vehicle, owned or jointly owned by a veteran... There is no fee for Ex-POW, Congressional Medal of Honor or Gold Star plates.

findings.name: Motor Vehicle Sales Tax and Registration Tax Exemption for Totally Disabled Veterans
findings.description: A veteran with a total service-connected disability is exempt from Minnesota's motor vehicle sales tax on a vehicle purchase (Minn. Stat. § 297B.03, cl. 16) and from motor vehicle registration tax, administrative/filing fees, and plate/validation sticker fees (Minn. Stat. § 168.012, subd. 13) on a passenger automobile, one-ton pickup, motorcycle, or recreational vehicle. The registration exemption applies to vehicles jointly registered with a spouse or domestic partner, and a qualifying veteran may register no more than two vehicles at a time under these exemptions; personalized-plate fees and required special-plate donations are not covered. As directly read in Minn. Stat. § 171.01, subd. 51, "veteran with a total service-connected disability" is defined as a 100 percent total and permanent VA service-connected disability rating — that statutory text does not mention Individual Unemployability (TDIU); some secondary (non-.gov) sources claim TDIU recipients also qualify, but that could not be confirmed against the statute text itself in this session, so it is flagged rather than stated as settled.
findings.value: Full exemption from motor vehicle sales tax; full exemption from registration tax and related fees (up to 2 vehicles)
otherReqs: 100 percent total and permanent VA service-connected disability rating
Applies to up to 2 vehicles, including jointly registered with a spouse/domestic partner
findings.agency: Minnesota Department of Public Safety, Driver and Vehicle Services (DVS)
documentation: VA certification of 100% total and permanent service-connected disability
findings.sourceExcerpt: a passenger automobile, one-ton pickup truck, motorcycle, or recreational vehicle registered by a veteran with a total service-connected disability, as defined in section 171.01, subdivision 51, is not subject to [registration taxes, administrative fees, filing fees and surcharges, plate and validation sticker fees]... A qualifying veteran may register no more than two motor vehicles at the same time with the exemptions under this subdivision.

findings.name: No-Fee and Reduced-Fee Hunting & Fishing Licenses for Disabled Veterans
findings.description: Minnesota residents who are veterans with a 100% service-connected disability (as defined by the VA) are issued, without fee, a permanent angling license, a deer license (firearms or archery), and a small game license (Minn. Stat. § 97A.441, subds. 5, 6, 6a); the DNR commissioner will issue a permanent card documenting the 100% status so it need not be re-verified each purchase. Separately, Minn. Stat. § 97A.465, subd. 9 (as directly read on revisor.mn.gov) creates a reduced-fee ($5, per Minn. Stat. § 97A.475) deer/small-game/angling license for veterans with a 50-99% service-connected disability — but that provision is not yet in effect: the statute text states it takes effect March 1, 2027, which is after this file's research date, so it should be treated as an upcoming rather than current benefit. Separately, residents discharged within the prior 24 months may take small game and fish without a license and receive one complimentary deer license of either sex (subd. 1b), and residents of Minnesota veterans homes have separate deer-license provisions (subd. 7).
findings.value: Free permanent deer, small game, and angling licenses for 100% disabled veterans; $5 reduced-fee deer/small-game/angling license for 50-99% disabled veterans (effective March 1, 2027)
otherReqs: Minnesota residency
100% tier: satisfactory evidence of 100% service-connected disability (permanent card or designated driver's license/ID)
50-99% tier: not in effect until March 1, 2027 per statute
documentation: VA certification of service-connected disability rating
DNR-issued permanent disability card, or driver's license/ID with disability designation
findings.sourceExcerpt: A person authorized to issue licenses must issue, without a fee, a permanent license to take fish by angling... a license to take deer with firearms or by archery... a license to take small game... to a resident who is a veteran, as defined in section 197.447, and that has a 100 percent service-connected disability as defined by the United States Veterans Administration

findings.name: Military Retirement Pay Subtraction (State Income Tax)
findings.description: Minnesota allows taxpayers to subtract qualifying military retirement pay (including pensions) from Minnesota taxable income and alternative minimum taxable income, claimed via Schedule M1M (Income Additions and Subtractions). Qualifying pay includes active-component retirement pay (10 U.S.C. §§ 1401-1414), reserve-component retirement pay (10 U.S.C. § 12733), and Survivor Benefit Plan payments (10 U.S.C. §§ 1447-1455); a divorced spouse who receives a portion of a former spouse's military pension may also subtract that share to the extent it is included in federal adjusted gross income. The subtraction cannot be combined with the separate Credit for Past Military Service, and pensions received solely from dual-status technician service do not qualify. The Department of Revenue's page does not state a specific dollar cap or percentage limit on the subtraction; it indicates the benefit generally provides greater value when federal AGI exceeds $37,500 or qualifying military pension pay totals $14,018 or more, but the exact underlying formula was not itemized on the fetched page.
findings.value: Subtraction of qualifying military retirement pay from Minnesota taxable income (no stated dollar cap found on official page)
otherReqs: Retirement pay must be taxable on the federal return
Cannot be combined with the Credit for Past Military Service
Pensions solely from dual-status technician service do not qualify
documentation: Federal tax return showing taxable military retirement pay
findings.sourceExcerpt: You may be able to subtract certain military retirement pay (including pensions) from your Minnesota taxable income and alternative minimum taxable income... Claim this subtraction by completing Schedule M1M, Income Additions and Subtractions.
